description: It's time to start talking about legislation for NEXT YEAR. If you have issues or ideas that impact HD37, please use the contact information below and let us know what we need to work on. Highlights of My Week at the Capitol This week's newsletter will be short and "to the point" as we're "burning the midnight oil" as we work with the Senate to negotiate the final pieces of legislation - our calendar is full including nights and weekends, so I have a bit less time to opine this week. As we come to the end of a very productive legislative session, all but one of my prime bills will be passing into law. In next week's newsletter, we will spend some time and recap the entire session. SB24-230 - Oil & Gas Fees To Support Transit This bill has passed through the legislature and will bolster accountability and sustainability within Colorado’s transit and energy sectors. It will establish fees to be collected from oil and gas producers will be used to pay for clean transit and wildlife and land remediation. The bill also mandates timely reporting and analysis of fee amounts, ensuring transparency and informed decision-making. HB24-1132 - The bill introduces the "CARE for Living Organ Donors Act," aimed at providing benefits and recognition for living organ donors. It includes provisions outlining benefits available to donors and requires transplant centers to inform potential donors about organ voucher programs. Additionally, the bill prohibits employers from retaliating against employees who become living organ donors and designates April 11 as "Living Organ Donor Recognition Day." Technical amendments to current law are also included in sections 2 and 4 of the bill. HB24-1373 - "Save Local Liquor Stores" Bill - The bill addresses regulations for alcohol beverage sales, including converting specific liquor-licensed drugstore licenses to fermented malt beverage and wine retailer licenses. It updates requirements for wholesalers and removes the cap on retailers' alcohol beverage purchases from retail liquor stores. Additionally, it prohibits retailers from displaying alcohol beverages in certain areas of the sales floor and expands delivery options between licensees. The bill also prohibits the sale of alcohol beverages with over seventeen percent alcohol by volume and includes an appropriation.
